minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 4, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:08
p.m., on October 4, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 1, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma (arrived at 5:20 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 6:09 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1.  Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission

City Council Minutes  1  October 4, 2010
   Viejo v. Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD), Case No. 00300610.

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he would like to continue this Closed Session
  item to the next meeting. The court has not yet entered the judgment so there is nothing
  affirmative to report at this time.

RECESS

At the hour of 5:10 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:05
p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Ury arrived at 6:09 p.m.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim October 3 through October 9, 2010 To Be Fire Prevention Week

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Battalion Chief Mike Ferdig.

P2.  Presentation by Duane Cave of San Diego Gas & Electric on Smart Meter
  Installation

  The City Council received the presentation from Duane Cave of San Diego Gas and
  Electric.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dan Avery, M.V.: stated that he was fortunate to be one of the sponsors of a recent candidate
forum and he encouraged residents to get out, meet the City Council candidates and really learn
who they are.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: announced that he challenged Mayor Kelley's candidate statement but the
City Clerk did not take action. He disputed Mayor Kelley's statement that she saved the Casta
del Sol golf course from development and he noted that in the future, any City Council majority
of three can change the zoning and housing can be built there.

Marvis Kushnick, M.V.: thanked the City Council for turning the courtyard area between city
hall and the library into a one-way drive. She stated that the library is the brightest star in
Mission Viejo's crown. She also, expressed her objection to the courtyard being closed in
December for Santa’s arrival and Santa's workshop.

John Maginnis, M.V.: thanked the city for partnering with the Friends of the Mission Viejo
Library to present the Readers’ Festival and he thanked the City Council Members who attended
the event.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: encouraged residents to consider how they want to vote in the next
election. She stated that negativity takes away from constructive business and impacts the

City Council Minutes  2  October 4, 2010
 efficiency of all of our city staff. She suggested residents focus on the positive and the future,
and consider those things when they vote.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 20, 2010, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register dated September 10, 2010, in the amount of $2,446,503.10

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Second Amendment to Cooperative Agreement C-9-0467 for Go Local Bus/Shuttle
  Service Planning

  Approved Second Amendment (A09-10B) to Cooperative Agreement C-9-0467 between
  the Orange County Transportation Authority and the City of Mission Viejo for Go Local
  Bus/Shuttle Service Planning.

5.  Removal and Replacement of the City of Mission Viejo Library and Civic Center /
  Saddleback Room Carpet and Flooring

  Approved the plans and specifications and authorized staff to obtain bids for the removal
  and replacement of the Library and Civic Center/Saddleback Room carpet and flooring.

6.  Grant Application for the Marguerite Parkway Median Island Civic Core
  Enhancement Project through OCTA Transportation Enhancement Act

City Council Minutes  3  October 4, 2010
   Adopted Resolution 10-55 Authorizing the Submittal of a Grant Application for Funds
  for the OCTA Transportation Enhancement (TE) Program Under the Jobs for 2005 Safe,
  Accountable, Flexible, Efficient Transportation Act.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

7.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

8.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the Foothill/Eastern
  TCA therefore she has nothing to report.

9.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San Joaquin
  Hills TCA therefore she has nothing to report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager's Report

City Attorney’s Report

10.  E-Verify Program Compliance for City Contracts

  City Attorney William Curley presented the report.

  By consensus, the City Council received the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

11.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  4  October 4, 2010
   The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma noted that things will be a little bit more spirited at the end of
October, prior to the election.

Council Member Schlicht

12.  Adoption of a Revolving Door Ordinance

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Dan Avery, M.V.: expressed concern with the item being placed on the agenda three
  times in a row and stated that this is just an election tactic.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that she is tired of city staff spending time on these things
  and that the majority of the Council has spoken on this matter. If an item is defeated, she
  believes the residents want the City Council to work on something more important.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to amend the Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  with the adoption of a Revolving Door Ordinance. The motion died for lack of a second.

Council Member Schlicht announced that a policy differs from an ordinance and the city’s
Revolving Door Policy has already failed when Dave Leckness, as a Planning Commissioner,
received purchase orders from the city. She wished Orange County Register reporter Niyaz
Pirani luck in his new job and she congratulated the Mission Viejo Dispatch blog on another
anniversary. Council Member Schlicht stated that the Dispatch provides the most complete news
for the community and the blog continues to grow and expand. She announced that the city has
great schools and, as an example, at last Friday’s football game, the Diablos won against Carson
in the first quarter. They also won the prior game, and whether or not the games are at home or
away, Mission Viejo always has the best attendance. Council Member Schlicht quoted President
Ford regarding respect for others’ principles and she stated that the Mayor has allowed the
Council Meetings to get out of hand and there is a total lack of respect. She noted that she was
elected on a watchdog premise and she is not going to let the negativity from others stop her
from defending the truth.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury stated that it’s an honor to serve on the City Council, to conduct business
in a very professional and forthright manner and it is an honor to make sure that the Council does
its best in terms of the will of the citizens. For him personally, it’s an honor to respect the office
of City Council Member but he feels that there are others who do not respect their official duties.

City Council Minutes  5  October 4, 2010
 Council Member Ury noted that the pressure is not coming from the dais but from the 100,000
residents that the Council serves. The community looks to the city for support with kids,
schools, traffic, public safety, and financial stewardship and that’s what the Council Members
and staff are charged with day in and day out. Council Member Ury discussed his attendance at
the Mission Viejo Readers’ Festival and stated that it was an absolutely amazing event. So many
cities have nothing in the way of programs and he challenged anyone to go live in another city
for 6 or 8 months to find out how lucky we really are.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that the Disney Store opening was fantastic. It is only the
4th store of its kind in the country and he encouraged residents to visit the store and see all that it
has to offer. He also discussed his attendance at the Readers’ Festival. It was a great, full day
and he congratulated staff on a job well done.

Mayor Kelley

13.  Whooping Cough Vaccination Clinic

  Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: stated that she contacted the Department of Health and they
  wanted to know if the city will be buying the vaccines. Mrs. Boyce asked if the nurses
  can conduct the vaccination clinic at the same time they administer flu shots on
  November 4.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to direct staff to
  gather the information and sponsor a whooping cough vaccination clinic in October as a
  service for our residents, to assist in preventing the illness and deaths in infants and
  children.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

Mayor Kelley complimented Deputy City Manager Karen Wylie on a very successful Business
Showcase. There were quite a number of Mission Viejo businesses represented and she thanked
those who attended. She also reiterated that the Readers’ Festival was a wonderful event. She
heard so many positive comments and she thanked the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library and
city staff for organizing such a successful day. She noted that events like this make Mission
Viejo unique and a special place to live. Mayor Kelley reminded residents to mark their
calendars for the Walk Against Drugs on October 23, 2010, beginning at 8:00 a.m. at Mission
Viejo High School. Participants will hear speakers and then walk to the Community Center for a
fair and Supervisor Pat Bates’ Emergency Preparedness Expo. She also encouraged residents

City Council Minutes  6  October 4, 2010
 sign up for the city’s eNewsletter and blog by visiting www.cityofmissionviejo.org. She stated
that residents can find accurate, clear and accountable information there and keep abreast of
what’s going on in the city with true and tested information. Mayor Kelley announced that the
Community of Character word for the month of October is respect and she reminded residents of
the monthly Films of Character. The next movie, The Jackie Robinson Story, will be shown on
October 17, in the City Council Chamber from 2:00 p.m. to 4:50 p.m. Finally, she thanked
Mission Viejo High School seniors for the blanket and she announced that they are conducting a
fundraiser for their grad night.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:29 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Shir Lee Spanjer and Lance Corporal Ralph
J. Fabree to Monday, October 18, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 18, 2010

City Council Minutes  7  October 4, 2010
